ram.time: Theta(n); constant-size query fields and amortized O(1) append
ram.auxiliary_space: O(1) excluding O(k) returned IDs and O(n) loaded catalogue
ram.count_convention: visits + evaluated predicate comparisons + output appends
ram.omitted_from_counts: loop mechanics, field loads, counter updates and interpreter instructions

external_memory.input_reads: ceil(n/B), cold aligned scan; B is records per block, M >= B
external_memory.output_writes: excluded; add O(1+k/B_out) if k result IDs are written externally
external_memory.layout: hypothetical contiguous fixed-size records, not Python objects or JSON bytes

cache_oblivious.input_transfers: O(1+n/B), without using B or M in the search algorithm
cache_oblivious.interpretation: sequential locality works across block sizes; no hardware misses were measured

parallel.implemented_baseline: W=Theta(n), S=Theta(n); sequential code has no parallel speedup
parallel.pram: synchronous shared-memory processors; constant-time word operations; ideal memory access
parallel.predicate_only: with p processors, ceil(n/p) record rounds up to constant predicate cost
parallel.compact_output: flags + work-efficient prefix sum + distinct-position scatter
parallel.parallel_design: W=Theta(n), S=Theta(log n), auxiliary space O(n), for n>=2
parallel.bounds: T_p >= max(W/p,S); an ideal greedy scheduler gives T_p <= W/p + S
parallel.parallelism: W/S=Theta(n/log n); full-query time O(n/p+log n) under the stated model
parallel.limitations: theory only; excludes scheduling, communication, bandwidth and Python overhead

equal_big_o: Two Theta(n) scans can have different constants, field layouts, cache misses, branch behavior, interpreter overhead and memory bandwidth. Predicate order also changes short-circuit work. Big O describes growth, not elapsed seconds.
